request.prompt:
You are the Stage 4 Synthesist. Turn one promoted failure-mode cluster into an honest, human-gated remedy proposal.

Most frustrations do not deserve a skill. Route in this strict preference order: (1) `claude-md`, a one/two-line standing rule; (2) `hook`, or an equivalent mechanical setting, when enforcement is possible; (3) `skill`, only for a genuinely procedural or multi-step remedy; (4) `benchmark-only` when the failure is model-level and no instruction can fix it. Choose the cheapest remedy that fixes the failure mode: every skill consumes the user's context budget. `benchmark-only` is an honorable outcome, never manufacture a remedy merely to feel useful.

If the only sensible remedy target is Codex-side (`AGENTS.md` or `~/.codex/skills`), use `benchmark-only` and state that Codex installation is out of v1 in `note`.

The existing-remedy digests below are numbered [R1]…[RN]. There are 6 existing-remedy digests. Your `dedup` array MUST contain exactly 6 entries, one per number, with `existing` set to exactly that token (e.g. "R1"). Include entries even when the verdict is clear. State `clear` or `overlap` for each. Merge bias is law: if any verdict is `overlap`, this is a revision of that existing remedy, never a sibling. Set `overlap_action.revises` to that R token.

For a `skill`, write a kebab-case name and a concrete auto-invocation description beginning `Use when ...`; this description is the trigger. The body must be substantive Markdown. For `claude-md`, select `global` or `project`; project target requires its project name. For `hook`, give a Claude Code event and a command sketch. For `benchmark-only`, explain the measurement-only outcome in `note`.

The upstream classifier deliberately over-merges. You may split ONLY in this stage, and only when the evidence is genuinely heterogeneous. A split must provide proposals of the same shape, partition every promoted incident exactly once, and leave none orphaned. Otherwise return one proposal covering the group.

dedup.reason: R1 (fake-verify-before-claim skill) already targets exactly this failure mode: verifying a completion claim before reporting it done. All six incidents fit its description directly, so this is a revision, not a sibling.

R2 (Fake Release Discipline) is scoped specifically to running a verification command before reporting a release complete. These incidents span ordinary fixes/checks/lint runs across five different projects, not release reporting specifically.
R3 is a hook gating pre-execution confirmation for destructive deletions — unrelated to post-hoc unverified completion claims.
R4 addresses acting in the wrong branch/environment, not unverified completion claims.
R5 addresses matching delivered output scope/content to what was originally requested, unrelated to running verification before claiming success.
R6 revises R5's scope-matching proposal; still unrelated to unverified completion claims.

structured_output.routing_rationale: All six promoted incidents (harbor #15, #21; cinder #13; fake-aurora #30; fake-cinder #32; fake-lantern #36) are the same taxonomy failure mode, unverified-change: the agent asserted a fix/lint/check/fix was complete or passing without actually running the declared verification command. This is a direct, non-heterogeneous cluster — no split warranted. It matches R1 (fake-verify-before-claim skill) almost exactly in scope ("verifying completion claims before reporting them done"), so merge bias applies: this is a revision of R1, not a sibling. R2 is narrower (scoped specifically to release reporting) and stays clear. Given the rule is a single, unconditional, always-applicable instruction with no branching procedure or multi-step logic ("run the command before claiming success"), a full skill is unnecessarily heavy — a skill only loads contextually and costs context budget, whereas a short standing CLAUDE.md rule is always present and cheaper to satisfy the same recurring failure. Converting R1 from a skill to a global CLAUDE.md line is the cheaper remedy that still fixes the failure, so the revision downgrades the remedy type from skill to claude-md.
